chunks: From him, from Dawud ibn Ishaq al-Hadhdha', from Muhammad ibn al-Fayd, who said:

I ate lentil broth with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'May I be your ransom, these people say that eighty prophets have sanctified lentils.' He said, 'They have lied, no, by Allah, not even twenty prophets.' And it is narrated that it softens the heart and hastens the flow of tears.

key_terms.مَرَقَةٍ: Broth or soup, specifically lentil soup in this context

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the claim that prophets sanctified lentils?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the popular folk belief that lentils were sanctified by eighty prophets, asserting that not even twenty prophets held them in special esteem, thereby distinguishing between cultural superstition and authentic prophetic tradition. This narration highlights the medicinal and spiritual properties of lentils, noting their ability to soften the heart and facilitate weeping, which aligns with the Shia emphasis on physical health as a means to spiritual humility and devotion.
